candidate.answerReason: The circles have centers 5 units apart and radii 7 and √(k+40). They share a point exactly for −36≤k≤104, including tangencies, so b−a=140.

methods.label: Compare the radii and center distance
methods.explanation:
Completing the squares reveals the centers and radii:
\[
(x-6)^2+(y-3)^2=49,
\]
\[
(x-2)^2+(y-6)^2=k+40.
\]
The first circle has center \((6,3)\) and radius \(7\). The second has center \((2,6)\), and the distance between the centers is
\[
\sqrt{(6-2)^2+(3-6)^2}=5.
\]
If \(k<-40\), the second graph has no real points. If \(k=-40\), it is only the point \((2,6)\), which is not on the first circle because its distance from the first center is \(5\), not \(7\).

For \(k>-40\), put \(r=\sqrt{k+40}>0\). Two circles share a point exactly when the center distance is at most the sum of the radii and at least their absolute difference. Equality includes external or internal tangency. Here these conditions are
\[
|7-r|\le5\le7+r.
\]
The right inequality is automatic because \(r>0\). The left gives \(2\le r\le12\). Since these bounds are nonnegative, squaring is equivalent and yields
\[
4\le k+40\le144,
\]
so \(-36\le k\le104\). Both endpoints give tangency and are included. Therefore
\[
b-a=104-(-36)=\boxed{140},
\]
choice D.
methods.levelReason: The method uses completing squares, the Pythagorean distance formula, and elementary circle-intersection conditions.

methods.label: Replace the second equation with a line
methods.explanation:
The two equations have the same left side, so subtracting them eliminates \(x^2+y^2\). Every common point must satisfy
\[
8x-6y+4-k=0.
\]
Conversely, any point satisfying this line equation and the first original equation also satisfies the second original equation, by reversing the subtraction. Thus the original graphs share a point exactly when this line meets the first circle.

Completing squares in the first equation gives
\[
(x-6)^2+(y-3)^2=49,
\]
whose center is \((6,3)\) and radius is \(7\). The perpendicular distance from this center to the line is
\[
\frac{|8(6)-6(3)+4-k|}{\sqrt{8^2+(-6)^2}}
=\frac{|34-k|}{10}.
\]
A line shares a point with a circle exactly when its distance from the center does not exceed the radius; equality gives tangency. Hence the necessary and sufficient condition is
\[
\frac{|34-k|}{10}\le7,
\]
or \(|k-34|\le70\). This is equivalent to
\[
-36\le k\le104.
\]
The subtraction was reversible, so every value in this interval gives a common point of the original graphs, including both endpoints, and no other value does. Therefore \(b-a=104-(-36)=\boxed{140}\), choice D.
methods.levelReason: This alternative uses school analytic geometry: subtracting equations, completing squares, and comparing a point-to-line distance with a circle's radius.
